o1.biggest_strength: Puts the in-app checkout bug first and sizes it correctly (about 560 extra orders, ₹34 lakh gross margin), then gives each test money, guardrails and a detection threshold.
o1.biggest_mistake: Test 5 bundles two changes (new hero image plus moving reviews) so a win tells you nothing about which change did it, and the A/A week is wasted at 0.56% conversion.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Split test 5 into one change, drop the A/A week, tighten the under-powered 2-week mobile sample sizes, and add a scannable ranked table up top.

o2.biggest_strength: Operationally complete: a ranked summary table, a two-lane factorial design with an interaction check, no-peek/ship rules, precise per-version sample sizes, and a fresh delivery-day-picker idea.
o2.biggest_mistake: Weakens the firmness signal (19% of chats) by folding it into review tabs instead of answering it directly, and leaves the EMI figure as a placeholder (₹X).
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Give firmness its own clear on-page answer backed by the real rating, and fill the EMI placeholder with the store's actual plan amounts.

reason: Both are strong and fix the bug first with sound money maths, but Output 2 is the one I'd hand my team: it reads faster, its sample sizes are exact, it handles test interaction, and it gives me a bolder delivery-day idea. Output 1's bundled hero-plus-reviews test means a win wouldn't tell me what worked.
